reason: The text describes and presents a clear hierarchical organizational structure for the Temple's reconstruction. Specific leaders are appointed with defined authority: Yeshua (the high priest) and Zerubbabel (political leader) stand at the top, with distinct roles for priests and Levites below them. The Levites are explicitly appointed (וַיַּעֲמִידוּ) to supervise the work (לְנַצֵּחַ - 'to oversee'), and age-based hierarchy is established (those twenty years and above). The text presents this organizational structure as the natural, proper, and necessary way to accomplish the sacred work, without suggesting alternatives. By narrating how hierarchy is established and functionally organized, the text implicitly endorses and reinforces hierarchical ordering as the appropriate framework for religious and community work.
